en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of these islands are actually inhabited.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano is the lowest volcano in the country, with its main crater located just 311 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, extending roughly 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground waterway that flows directly through a cave into the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippine Eagle is one of the largest eagles globally, boasting a wingspan of up to two meters and a shaggy crest.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares and protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones each year, with the majority striking the country between June and November.
The Philippines has vast mineral resources, holding the second-largest gold deposits globally and ranking as a top producer of nickel.
Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte drops 98 meters down two separate cascades to generate hydroelectric power for Mindanao.
